<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided file is a patch for the cdw package, modifying calls to `mvwprintw` in several source files to explicitly use the `%s` format specifier when printing string variables. This change addresses proper format string usage in C, preventing potential vulnerabilities if the string content were ever to contain format specifiers like `%n` or `%x`.

The modifications are straightforward and localized to improving code safety by ensuring that user-controlled or dynamically generated strings are printed safely. There is no evidence of malicious intent, obfuscated code, unauthorized network activity, or unexpected system modifications. The changes align with standard C programming best practices for secure coding.

Such patches are common in open-source projects to harden code against format string vulnerabilities, especially when string contents might be influenced by external input. In this context, the patch improves security without introducing any risks.
</details>
<evidence>
